women-writers-in-global-south-climate-ca.headline: Women Writers In Global South - Climate, Care & Environmental Justice
women-writers-in-global-south-climate-ca.author: Zoë Brigley Thompson
women-writers-in-global-south-climate-ca.core: Posted in last 7 days Women Writers In Global South - Climate, Care & Environmental Justice On 10 November, UN Women released Gender Equality in the Age of Climate Crisis at COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye. I’ve been thinking about what the facts gathered here mean for the daily lives of women and girls in places already facing disasters... In the worst-case scenario, ecological emergency could push up to 141 million more women and girls into extreme poverty by 2050! The fact sheet also reports that a rise of 1°C in average temperatures is associated with women losing 34 per cent more of their income than men. After disasters, women and girls often take on more unpaid care, looking after family members. The fact sheet suggests (from research across 14 countries) that disasters make for a higher possibility of experiencing sexual violence, especially for teenage girls and younger women. Finally, in 2024, an estimated 326 million women and girls, most of them in the Global South, lived without electricity. At the same time, sickeningly, expansion of AI is driving up electricity demand from data centres. I find it hard to know what to say about poetry, literature and books in the face of all this. Sometimes it feels almost irrelevant. As an editor though, I hope I can make more room for writing about it, because we need to witness what is happening. I’d especially like to hear from women writing from or with ties to the Global South (which is being impacted most). I am wondering if those writers might explore ecological change, care, and environmental justice in their own communities. When Poetry Wales next opens for submissions, I’d love to see poems or articles that come out of those experiences and questions. MODRON is open to article pitches now, and I’d be glad to hear what you’d like to write about. We consider each submission on its own terms, and I’d love to see what you’re working on. I also want to be upfront that MODRON doesn’t currently have funding to pay contributors - we hope this will change in future! If you’re interested, a few lines about what you’d like to write are plenty for an initial pitch. https://lnkd.in/eu9mQYZK Here is the link news on the UN Women fact sheet too: https://lnkd.in/e_EwSdD6 Poetry Wales
